cases.title: Eclipse investment versus frontline packages
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: On a level-9 Aphelios board, when is keeping Eclipse worth the slots compared with a stronger frontline and utility package? Does that change if the Solar units are already three-star?
cases.question: On a level-9 Aphelios board, when is keeping Eclipse worth the slots compared with a stronger frontline and utility package? Does that change if the Solar units are already three-star?
cases.scenario: Final level-nine itemized Aphelios; active Eclipse versus alternative named frontline/utility packages, split explicit Solar-unit three-star vectors from predominantly two-star variants.
cases.plan: Discover support packages rather than fixing Kennen/Amumu or Sentinel/Taric as complete boards. Compare recorded active Eclipse and its complement within shared carry/level/star shells, and compare named alternative packages where expressible. Query Solar member stars and verify actual Eclipse activation independently.
cases.checks: Report the Eclipse contrast inside each declared Solar upgrade vector and associated support substitutions, with counts/outcomes and uncertainty. Do not infer Eclipse from generic Solar presence or claim a causal benefit of spending slots.
cases.limits: No generic all-three-star or no-three-star-legendary filter; enumerate named vectors or mark incompleteness. Generic Lux identity and global investment equality need additional certification.

cases.title: Two caps for Azir and Mama Beak
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: For a level-8 Azir–Mama Beak board, how do the Ezreal–Scuttle Crab and Kennen–Amumu versions compare as finished boards? Is one more likely to win rather than just make top four?
cases.question: For a level-8 Azir–Mama Beak board, how do the Ezreal–Scuttle Crab and Kennen–Amumu versions compare as finished boards? Is one more likely to win rather than just make top four?
cases.scenario: Level-eight itemized Azir/Mama Beak, primary Rapidfire Emblem on Azir, comparing Ezreal+Scuttlecrab versus Kennen+Amumu. Known common units include Krug, Sett and Yunara; the original sixth common unit is unknown.
cases.plan: Use the five known shared anchors and the emblem-holder constraint as a discovery shell. Query companion-unit frequencies and verify supported sixth-unit conjunctions separately for both candidate pairs, keeping one pair absent in the other arm. Compare matched discovered-sixth-unit package cells when available. After a sixth common identity is observed and verified, requiring all eight distinct names and selecting a reportable board_size=8 query row can certify stored-roster closure for its own outcomes. It does not recover the original image roster or confer a filtered compare_cohorts interval.
cases.checks: Do not invent the sixth unit or present a contains-seven-units shell as a certified exact eight-unit roster. Report observed completion candidates and pair-specific counts/top4/win, with carry/Krug upgrades and utility item differences. Win rate and top4 can favor different caps.
cases.limits: The original image-based exact roster cannot be recovered from code. Current-query cohorts are explicitly a reconstruction study unless complete legal rosters are independently certified; level eight is not an exact unit-count predicate. Alpha Mark remains unobserved.

cases.title: Popular Primal cap versus observed performance
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: TFT Codex lists several level-nine Primal Aphelios–Nidalee finishes. Is the most popular last unit also getting the best placements and win rate?
cases.question: For level-nine Primal Aphelios–Nidalee end boards in the scoped data, is the most common finishing unit also getting the best average placement and win rate? Compare the Alune, Brambleback and Ivern versions around the shared core.
cases.scenario: Shared eight: Amumu, Aphelios, Nidalee, Sentinel, Diana, Kog'Maw, Vi and Varus. Inspect Alune, Brambleback and Ivern additions at final level nine with candidate overlap separated; inventory/star differences remain visible.
cases.plan: Use three explicit contains-core-plus-candidate cohorts; query board_size to inspect the nine-unit-record slice descriptively, because final level alone does not close a roster. Get candidate counts and outcomes through query_cohort/compare_cohorts, then compare popularity ordering separately from mean-placement and win-rate ordering. For the fully enumerated 9-identity roster, query_cohort grouped by board_size can expose a reportable row equal to 9; that row establishes no extra or duplicate stored identities and supplies its own sample/outcomes. Keep these exact-record results separate from broader compare_cohorts summaries and intervals.
cases.checks: Rank the three inspected options from actual counts/metrics with explicit denominators. A reportable nine-record row after requiring all nine distinct names certifies stored-roster closure for that row; otherwise retain the broader contains-core qualification and overlap diagnostics. The answer need not reproduce the old Alune-most-popular/Brambleback-best result. Do not turn a final-state association into a replacement recommendation.
cases.limits: Exact contains-only roster/extra-slot control and an exhaustive eligible ninth-unit pool are not available by a single filter. Named-candidate coverage is explicit; public results may differ from the archived web panel. No direct exact-roster filter does not mean closure is impossible: the 9-required-identities/9-record grouped-row route is supported when the row is reportable. It certifies stored identities, not occupied capacity or legal deployment.
cases.adaptation: Removed dependence on a mutable TFT Codex panel while preserving the popularity-versus-performance investigation and its known shared roster. Original website snapshot numbers remain historical provenance, not gold for a different database.

cases.title: How clear is the legendary cap ranking?
cases.subject: compositions
cases.original_question: The level-ten Elder Dragon–Draven options on TFT Codex look very close. Is there convincing evidence that the Alune version is better than the Lux or Soraka versions?
cases.question: For level-ten Elder Dragon–Draven end boards in the scoped data, is there convincing evidence that the Alune support version performs better than the Lux or Soraka versions, once the shared core and observed investment differences are considered?
cases.scenario: Shared eight unit records: Draven, Elder Dragon, Ivern, Kennen, Maokai, Taric, Amumu and Sentinel, plus Alune, Lux or Soraka. Elder Dragon uses two occupied slots in the reference; nine records do not mean a level-nine board.
cases.plan: Compare explicit candidate support cohorts at final level ten within named carry/tank star/loadout strata. Query board_size and other companions for roster diagnostics. Inspect compare_cohorts effect intervals and overlap; use resolvable Lux variants or label generic-Lux heterogeneity. For the fully enumerated 9-identity roster, query_cohort grouped by board_size can expose a reportable row equal to 9; that row establishes no extra or duplicate stored identities and supplies its own sample/outcomes. Keep these exact-record results separate from broader compare_cohorts summaries and intervals.
cases.checks: Report each sample, mean/top4/win and pairwise uncertainty from current returned results. Small rounded differences or an interval spanning zero do not establish either superiority or equivalence. A high selected end-state win rate is not the chance of winning after choosing the composition.
cases.limits: Exact occupied capacity and complete roster closure are not public filters. No gold ordering or old panel percentages are carried over, and unresolved Lux variants limit comparability. No direct exact-roster filter does not mean closure is impossible: the 9-required-identities/9-record grouped-row route is supported when the row is reportable. It certifies stored identities, not occupied capacity or legal deployment.
cases.adaptation: Converted the website-panel interpretation into a ChatTFT scoped-data uncertainty comparison, keeping the shared core and three alternatives. The previously supported web-only answer is not considered measured support for this new benchmark.
